topicName: InnoDB Storage Layout and File Formats
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"InnoDB Storage Layout and File Formats in MySQL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Understanding how InnoDB structures data on disk is crucial for database administrators and performance engineers. This tutorial explores the architecture of InnoDB tablespaces, pages, extents, and the evolution of its file formats."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. The InnoDB Storage Hierarchy"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"InnoDB stores data in a hierarchical storage structure composed of tablespaces, segments, extents, and pages. At the lowest level of physical storage is the page, and at the highest logical level is the tablespace."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pages: The fundamental unit of InnoDB disk storage. The default page size is 16KB, but it can be configured to 4KB, 8KB, 32KB, or 64KB."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Extents: A collection of contiguous pages, typically consisting of 64 consecutive pages (1MB in a default 16KB page setup)."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Segments: Collections of extents that are allocated for specific data structures, such as B-tree leaf nodes (data) or non-leaf nodes (indexes)."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Tablespaces: The highest logical container, which can be system tablespaces, file-per-table tablespaces, or general tablespaces."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. File-Per-Table Spaces and Innodb File Formats"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern versions of MySQL use the Barracuda file format by default, which supports advanced features like row compression and dynamic page storage. You can check your current file format and tablespace settings using SQL queries."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"SELECT TABLE_NAME, ROW_FORMAT, FILE_SIZE, DATA_FREE FROM information_schema.INNODB_TABLESPACES WHERE NAME LIKE 'myschema/%';"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Analyzing Page Layout"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Every 16KB data page in InnoDB contains a standard layout split into several parts: File Header, Page Header, Infimum and Supremum Records, User Records, Free Space, and File Trailer. The File Header contains checksums and page sequence numbers, while the File Trailer guarantees data integrity during unexpected shutdowns."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Inspecting Storage Layout via Performance Schema"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"To inspect the internal buffer pool utilization and monitor how pages are cached and read from disk, you can query the InnoDB buffer pool metadata tables."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"SELECT POOL_ID, DATA_LOCKED, DATABASE_NAME, TABLE_NAME, NUMBER_RECORDS FROM information_schema.INNODB_BUFFER_PAGE WHERE TABLE_NAME IS NOT NULL LIMIT 10;"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Proper management of InnoDB storage layout, page sizes, and file formats helps optimize I/O performance, reduce fragmentation, and ensure high availability in production MySQL environments."}]
